answer: A memory-bound protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to hold lookup tables anchored to a walnut state tree. Validators issue fast memory probes, leaving no haven for virtualized clones that swap storage dynamically. An attacker must dedicate scarce physical RAM per identity rather than time-sharing hardware. Auditors treat anomalous read latency as a diagnostic pigment signaling fraud. However, memory bus contention can falsely penalize honest nodes under heavy workloads.
